open_points.subject: AuditRecord creation for failed significant operations
open_points.text: State 0 says, “An action is recorded when it completes or, for a snapshot import, when the attempt is classified; an operation that fails on storage or the Registry before that is not recorded (R0-25).” M36 says, “every significant action — an action of the closed audit action catalog (State 2) — writes exactly one record,” including expense changes, progress updates, payment registration, photo changes, budget edits and version activation; State 0 invariant 12 also says, “Every significant action carries actor provenance to audit.”
open_points.question: When a catalogued significant operation other than snapshot import fails because Registry or storage fails before the business operation completes, must it create a rejected AuditRecord or create no AuditRecord?
options: Create no AuditRecord for any pre-completion Registry or storage failure
Create exactly one rejected AuditRecord because the attempted operation is a significant catalogued action
open_points.default_guess: Create no AuditRecord, following the new explicit exception in State 0.

witness.initial: An active Registry project has an existing Expense, and an active assigned operator has expense-management capability.
events: The operator submits a correction to the Expense.
The portal's Registry check times out before the correction completes.
outcomes: No business record changes and no AuditRecord is created, because the operation failed on Registry before completion.
No business record changes, but one rejected expense-correction AuditRecord is created, because M36 requires exactly one record for every significant expense change action.
witness.observer: An administrator or auditor reading the audit history sees either no attempted correction or a rejected correction.
